availability: SkinVision has partnerships with health insurers, cancer clinics, and research universities in the United Kingdom, Australia, Germany, the Netherlands, and New Zealand, and skin checks may be covered by a user's health insurance provider. The service is not yet available in the United States; U.S. launch is planned pending applicable regulatory clearance.
summary: SkinVision is a health technology company focused on increasing access to skin health awareness and care. It supports individuals in becoming more aware of their skin over time, helping them take a more active role in their health journey. The service is currently not available in the United States, pending regulatory clearance.
medicalPurpose: To increase access to skin health awareness and care, and to support individuals in becoming more aware of their skin over time.
acceptableInput: A smartphone photo of a skin spot or mole.
output: A risk indication for the most common types of skin cancer, delivered within 30–60 seconds, with a recommendation on next steps, including whether to see a healthcare professional.
roleInDecisionMaking: To help individuals take a more active role in their skin health journey by increasing awareness and accessibility to information.
intendedUsers: Individuals seeking to increase their awareness and understanding of their skin health.
targetPatientPopulation: The target patient population includes individuals and people seeking to increase their skin health awareness and care, become more aware of their skin over time, and take a more active role in their health journey.
knownPerformanceLimitations: SkinVision is not yet available in the United States; U.S. availability is subject to FDA authorization and U.S. launch is planned pending applicable regulatory clearance.
requiredClinicianOversight: SkinVision is not intended to replace traditional methods for evaluating skin cancer risk, does not provide a diagnosis, and is not a substitute for visits to a healthcare professional.
modelType: AI-based algorithm for skin cancer risk assessment, combining smartphone image analysis with oversight from dermatologists.

modelDevelopmentAndValidation.description: The company collaborates with medical experts, researchers, and leading institutions, including Mayo Clinic, for ongoing research and development in digital health.

performance.summary: The SkinVision algorithm has a sensitivity greater than 90% in detecting the three most common types of skin cancer (malignant melanoma, squamous cell carcinoma, and basal cell carcinoma) and a specificity of 89%, measured on SkinVision's user population. Users have received more than 3.5 million risk assessments, and the service has identified over 50,000 cases of melanoma and other skin cancers.

ongoingMonitoringPlan: SkinVision invests in ongoing research and clinical evidence collection, supported by a quality system involving dermatologists worldwide, to maintain and improve the reliability and accuracy of its risk-assessment service.
